'''Elena Cattaneo''' {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic|OMRI]]}} ({{IPA|it|ˈɛːlena katˈtaːneo}}; born 22 October 1962) is an [[Italian people|Italian]] [[pharmacology|pharmacologist]] and co-founding director of the [[University of Milan]]'s Center for Stem Cell Research.

She is a known Huntington's disease researcher and stem cell research advocate.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/business/biotech/sd-me-serbin-pope-20170507-story.html|title=Pope Francis meets with Huntington's patients, including University of San Diego scholar|last=Fikes|first=Bradley J.|work=sandiegouniontribune.com|access-date=2018-02-03|language=en-US}}</ref> She is internationally recognised for her commitment to research ethics and research policy, and for increasing knowledge and engagement in research among the general public.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cattaneo |first=Elena |date=January 2011 |title=Science and politics. An interview with Elena Cattaneo, Director of the Centre for Stem Cell Research at the University of Milano, Italy. Interview by Marta Paterlini |journal=EMBO Reports |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=23–26 |doi=10.1038/embor.2010.194 |issn=1469-3178 |pmc=3024131 |pmid=21132018}}</ref>

On 30 August 2013, she was appointed [[Senator for life#Italy|senator for life]] in the Italian Parliament.

==Biography==
Cattaneo was born in [[Milan]]. After graduating (summa cum laude) in pharmacy in 1986, she moved to [[Boston]] in the [[United States]] for a few years, where she specialized at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ilsole24ore.com/art/tecnologie/2013-03-06/elena-cattaneo-165948.shtml?uuid=Abo0iWbH |title=Elena Cattaneo |work=Il Sole 24 Ore |access-date=31 August 2013}}</ref> She studied neural stem cell differentiation in the area of the human brain associated with degenerative diseases under Professor [[Ronald McKay]]. Another of her mentors was Professor [[Anders Björklund]] of the [[University of Lund]]. Cattanaeo spent a short time with him in Sweden learning grafting techniques that could be used on stem cells.<ref name=unimi>[http://users2.unimi.it/labcattaneo/wordpress-eng/?page_id=42 Prof Elena Cattaneo] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810030302/http://users2.unimi.it/labcattaneo/wordpress-eng/?page_id=42 |date=10 August 2016 }}, Unimi.it. Retrieved 10 August 2015</ref> Returning to Italy she started her academic career in the [[University of Milan]]. She lived in [[Brugherio]] and worked in Milan.<ref name=brug>[http://www.mbnews.it/2013/08/e-di-brugherio-la-nuova-senatrice-a-vita-elena-cattaneo/ Life senator], MBNews. Retrieved 9 August 2015</ref> 

She is now full professor at the Laboratory of Stem Cell Biology and Pharmacology of Neurodegenerative Diseases in the Department of Biosciences of University of Milan.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.4-traders.com/news/The-Alliance-for-Regenerative-Medicine-Releases-Agenda-for-2016-Cell-Gene-Meeting-on-the-Mesa--23016552/|title=The Alliance for Regenerative Medicine : Releases Agenda for 2016 Cell & Gene Meeting on the Mesa|last=4-traders|access-date=2018-02-03}}</ref>
[[File:Napolitano and Cattaneo.jpg|left|thumb|Former President Napolitano and Senator Cattaneo]]
Cattaneo was appointed to the [[Senate of Italy]] as a [[Senator for life]], the youngest in Italian history, by then President [[Giorgio Napolitano]] on 30 August 2013, along with [[Claudio Abbado]], [[Renzo Piano]] and [[Carlo Rubbia]].<ref name=huff4>[http://www.huffingtonpost.it/2013/08/30/senatori-a-vita-abbado-piano-rubbia-cattaneo_n_3841906.html Giorgio Napolitano nomina Claudio Abbado, Renzo Piano, Carlo Rubbia e Elena Cattaneo senatori a vita], ''The Huffington Post'', August 2013, in Italian. Retrieved 10 August 2015</ref> Of his choice of her as Senator for Life, President Napolitano said: "choosing her is meant as an appreciation and an encouragement for many Italians of the new generations who commit themselves, amid difficulties, to scientific research".<ref>[http://www.ipscell.com/2013/10/stem-cell-person-of-the-year-2013-elena-cattaneo/ Stem Cell Person of the Year 2013: Elena Cattaneo], ipcell.com. Retrieved 10 August 2015</ref>

Cattaneo has used her position to oppose unfounded claims made by companies offering stem cell remedies.<ref>[http://www.nature.com/news/stem-cells-taking-a-stand-against-pseudoscience-1.15408 Stems Cells taking a stand against pseudoscience], Elena Cattaneo& Gilberto Corbellini, ''Nature'', 16 June 2014. Retrieved 10 August 2015</ref> The scientifically unsupported claims were primarily being made by a private well-connected company called the Stamina Foundation which had been started in 2009. The [[Stamina therapy]] involved recommending stem cells for a range of conditions with little or no scientific proof of their efficacy. Journalists including prestigious employees of the journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' were lied to and threatened. The scientific community's consensus was against Stamina. Stamina took advantage of the well meaning supporters of very ill people who believed that Stamina's claims was their only hope.<ref name=rightvmight/>

In 2012 the debate appeared to be settled when the Italian Medicines Agency declared Stamina's methods unsafe, however the Foundation appealed to their supporters and they appealed to the politicians and the courts. The courts cited compassion as the reason that they gave in to many of the 450 appeals who demanded the courts should allow patients to receive the stem cell "panacea". Some politicians went further and used government money to fund a multi-million-pound trial. It was not until August 2014 that a court in Turin demanded that not only should Stamina stop but their equipment should also be confiscated. This was possible because of the support of Cattaneo, a senator.<ref name=rightvmight/> As soon as Cattaneo became a senator she used her senatorial powers to demand evidence against Stamina that others had been denied. January 2014 saw the beginning of 25 hearings by the 15-strong enquiry.<ref name=rightvmight/> The eventual enquiry report demanded a number of points including that courts should always have scientific representation in cases of this sort.<ref name=rightvmight>{{cite journal|title=When right beat might|journal=Nature|date=24 February 2015|doi=10.1038/518455a|pmid=25719626|volume=518|issue=7540|pages=455|bibcode=2015Natur.518..455.|doi-access=free}}</ref> It was reported that the "Stamina case ... shows the influence that individual scientists can have in fighting anti-science forces."<ref name=rightvmight/>

Cattaneo has also been awarded the ''Medaglia teresiana'' by the [[University of Pavia]], in 2013. In 2015, ''Nature'' dedicated an editorial to laud the work that Cattaneo and her supporters had achieved.<ref name=rightvmight/> 

In 2016, Cattaneo helped raising concerns about three anti-GMO papers by Federico Infascelli at the [[University of Naples Federico II|University of Naples]], which were later retracted from [[Nature (journal)|Nature]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dailykos.com/stories/2016/03/15/1501856/-Another-anti-GMO-article-retracted-shocking-news|title=Another anti-GMO article retracted – shocking news|work=Daily Kos|access-date=2018-02-03}}</ref> Nature News reported that Cattaneo found that certain images in those papers had been deleted or tampered with, and that some images in different studies were identical, despite captions claiming that they were the results of novel experiments. Her suspicions led to an investigation by the University of Naples, which also found evidence of data manipulation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/45113/title/GM-Paper-Flagged-by-Politician-Retracted/|title=GM Paper Flagged by Politician Retracted|website=The Scientist|access-date=2018-02-03}}</ref>

In 2017, Cattaneo and Ignacio Munoz-Sanjuan organized the event HD as part of a campaign called HDdennomore, pronounced "Hidden no more" (HD is an acronym for the [[Huntington's disease]]), which aims to relieve families of the stigma of the disease, particularly those in poor communities in South America where the condition is most common.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2017/may/27/huntingtons-disease-pope-steps-in-to-raise-awareness|title=Huntington's disease: the pope steps in to help raise awareness|last=Mohammadi|first=Dara|date=2017-05-27|website=the Guardian|language=en|access-date=2018-02-03}}</ref> The event was brought about after Cattaneo wrote to [[Pope Francis]] last summer and asked him to meet with someone with the disease.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.inquisitr.com/4232534/pope-francis-says-that-embryos-should-never-be-used-in-research-not-even-to-fight-incurable-diseases/|title=Pope Francis Says That Embryos Should Never Be Used In Research, Not Even To Fight Incurable Diseases|date=2017-05-20|work=The Inquisitr|access-date=2018-02-03|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2018, Cattaneo was selected to be a new honorary doctor at the Faculty of Medicine at [[Lund University]]. Cattaneo has strong links to the research field at Lund University, where she spent time conducting research since the 1990s, and has continued since then.{{fact|date=June 2018}}
